questions.q: A 35-year-old farmer presents with a painless ulcer on his right hand that started as a papule 2 weeks ago. The ulcer has a black eschar with surrounding edema. He had contact with animal hides recently. Which of the following is the most likely causative organism?
questions.exp: Cutaneous anthrax caused by Bacillus anthracis classically presents as a painless ulcer with a black eschar (malignant pustule) and surrounding edema. History of contact with animal hides or wool is characteristic.

questions.q: A 28-year-old patient presents with recurrent episodes of grouped vesicles on an erythematous base over the genitalia for the past 6 months. The lesions heal spontaneously in 10-14 days. Tzanck smear shows multinucleated giant cells. Which antiviral would you prescribe for suppressive therapy?
questions.exp: For suppressive therapy of recurrent genital herpes, Valacyclovir 500 mg once daily is the preferred regimen due to better bioavailability and simpler dosing. Acyclovir 400 mg BD is an alternative but less convenient.

questions.q: A 22-year-old male presents with multiple hypopigmented patches over the trunk with fine scales. KOH examination shows 'spaghetti and meatballs' appearance. The most appropriate first-line treatment for extensive involvement is:
opts: Oral itraconazole 200 mg daily for 7 days
Selenium sulfide shampoo weekly for 4 weeks
questions.exp: Pityriasis versicolor due to Malassezia furfur shows characteristic 'spaghetti and meatballs' on KOH. For extensive disease, oral itraconazole 200 mg/day for 7 days is effective. Fluconazole 300-400 mg weekly for 2-4 weeks is also used.

questions.q: A 45-year-old immunocompromised patient develops painful vesicular eruption along T5-T6 dermatome on the right side. Three days later he develops an ipsilateral lower motor neuron facial palsy with vesicles in the external auditory canal. This syndrome is caused by:
questions.exp: Ramsay Hunt syndrome (Herpes Zoster Oticus) is caused by VZV reactivation in the geniculate ganglion of the facial nerve (CN VII). It presents with ipsilateral LMN facial palsy, vesicles in the external auditory canal/pinna, and otalgia.

questions.q: A 30-year-old sexual worker presents with painless, indurated ulcer over the labia with non-tender inguinal lymphadenopathy. Dark-field microscopy reveals spiral organisms. Which test will be most useful to assess treatment response?
questions.exp: VDRL (non-treponemal test) titres are used to monitor treatment response in syphilis as they decline with successful treatment. FTA-ABS and TPHA are treponemal tests that remain positive for life and cannot be used to monitor treatment.

questions.q: A 25-year-old male presents with painless groove sign (groove sign of Greenblatt) over the inguinal region with bilateral tender lymphadenopathy. He had an episode of genital ulcer 3 weeks ago which healed spontaneously. The most likely diagnosis is:
questions.exp: Lymphogranuloma venereum (LGV) caused by C. trachomatis L1-L3 serovars presents with the groove sign (groove between inguinal and femoral lymph nodes divided by inguinal ligament). The primary ulcer is transient and painless.

questions.q: A 40-year-old male from a rural area presents with loss of sensation over a hypopigmented patch over the cheek, thickened greater auricular nerve, and claw hand deformity. Slit skin smear shows bacterial index of 4+. According to WHO classification, what is the treatment regimen?
questions.exp: This is multibacillary (MB) leprosy (BI ≥2+ or more than 5 patches). MB-MDT consists of Rifampicin 600mg monthly, Clofazimine 300mg monthly + 50mg daily, Dapsone 100mg daily for 12 months as per current WHO guidelines.

questions.q: A leprosy patient on treatment develops sudden onset painful erythematous nodules over the face and limbs, fever, and iritis. Which of the following is the most appropriate treatment?
questions.exp: Erythema Nodosum Leprosum (ENL) with severe systemic involvement (iritis) is best treated with Thalidomide 400 mg/day in males. It is contraindicated in females of childbearing age due to teratogenicity. Prednisolone is used for Type 1 reactions and mild ENL.

questions.q: A 35-year-old female with photosensitive rash over the malar area, discoid lesions, oral ulcers, and arthritis. ANA is 1:640, anti-dsDNA is strongly positive. She develops frothy urine. Which antibody is most specifically associated with renal involvement in this condition?
questions.exp: Anti-dsDNA antibodies are the most specific antibodies for SLE and their titres correlate with disease activity, especially lupus nephritis. Anti-Sm is most specific for SLE diagnosis but not for monitoring activity.

questions.q: A 55-year-old female presents with progressive dysphagia, Raynaud's phenomenon, calcinosis cutis over fingers, and telangiectasias. Anti-centromere antibody is positive. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: CREST syndrome (limited systemic sclerosis) is characterized by Calcinosis, Raynaud's, Esophageal dysmotility, Sclerodactyly, Telangiectasia. Anti-centromere antibodies are positive in 70-80% of limited SSc. Pulmonary hypertension is a major complication.

questions.q: A 60-year-old male presents with tense bullae over the trunk and extremities. Nikolsky sign is negative. Direct immunofluorescence shows linear IgG and C3 deposition along the basement membrane zone. The autoantigen is:
questions.exp: Bullous pemphigoid is characterized by tense bullae, negative Nikolsky sign, and linear IgG/C3 at BMZ on DIF. The major autoantigen is BP180 (BPAG2/Collagen XVII, NC16A domain). BP230 (BPAG1) is the other autoantigen.

questions.q: A 45-year-old female presents with flaccid bullae and erosions over the oral mucosa and scalp. Nikolsky sign is positive. DIF shows intercellular IgG deposits in a 'chicken-wire/fish-net' pattern. The primary pathogenic antibody targets:
questions.exp: Pemphigus vulgaris (mucosal dominant type) involves oral mucosa primarily. Anti-Desmoglein 3 antibodies are responsible for mucosal lesions. Anti-Dsg1 antibodies cause skin lesions. The desmoglein compensation hypothesis explains the clinical phenotype.

questions.q: A 70-year-old male presents with a pearly, translucent papule with telangiectasias over the nasal ala with central ulceration. He is a chronic sun-exposed farmer. The most important initial treatment is:
questions.exp: Basal cell carcinoma at the nasal ala (H-zone, high-risk area) requires Mohs micrographic surgery for highest cure rate with maximum tissue conservation. Mohs surgery is preferred for high-risk sites (face, especially H-zone) and recurrent lesions.

questions.q: A 35-year-old male presents with an asymmetric pigmented lesion over the back measuring 2 cm with irregular borders, multiple colors (black, brown, red), and recent changes. Dermoscopy shows atypical pigment network, regression structures, and blue-white veil. Sentinel lymph node biopsy shows micrometastasis. What is the T stage?
questions.exp: Melanoma staging (AJCC 8th ed): T1 ≤1mm, T2 1.01-2mm, T3 2.01-4mm, T4 >4mm. 'a'=no ulceration, 'b'=ulceration. A 2cm lesion would be classified based on Breslow thickness not surface size. For Breslow thickness 1.01-2mm without ulceration, it's T2a. SLNB positive = Stage III.

questions.q: A 50-year-old male with a 10-year history of psoriasis presents with multiple tender joints of fingers and toes, sausage-like swelling of entire digits, and nail pitting. Radiograph shows 'pencil-in-cup' deformity. Which biologic targets TNF-alpha?
questions.exp: Adalimumab is a fully human anti-TNF-α monoclonal antibody approved for both psoriasis and psoriatic arthritis. Ustekinumab targets IL-12/23, Secukinumab targets IL-17A, Guselkumab targets IL-23p19.

questions.q: A 25-year-old presents with extensive plaque psoriasis (PASI 30) failing topical treatment. She is planning pregnancy in 6 months. Which systemic agent is the safest option?
questions.exp: Cyclosporine is the safest systemic agent in psoriasis for a woman planning pregnancy. Methotrexate requires 3-month washout before conception, Acitretin requires 3-year washout (due to storage in fat), and MMF is teratogenic. Cyclosporine can be stopped 1 month before conception.

questions.q: A 3-year-old child is brought with intensely pruritic eruption over the face, neck, and flexures. Mother has bronchial asthma. IgE levels are elevated. Skin examination shows lichenification with excoriations. Which of the following is a major criterion for diagnosis of atopic dermatitis?
questions.exp: According to Hanifin and Rajka criteria, PRURITUS is a major criterion for atopic dermatitis ('itch that rashes'). Other major criteria include typical morphology/distribution, chronic relapsing course, and personal/family atopy history.

questions.q: A patient presents with well-defined, erythematous, scaly plaques with papular borders over elbows and knees with silvery scales. Scratching reveals Auspitz sign. Which is the most accurate test to confirm the histopathological diagnosis?
opts: Presence of spongiform pustule of Kogoj
Parakeratosis with loss of granular layer
All of the above on biopsy
questions.exp: Parakeratosis with absence/loss of granular layer is the hallmark histological feature of psoriasis. Munro microabscesses (neutrophils in stratum corneum) and Kogoj's spongiform pustule (in spinous layer) are supportive features, but parakeratosis with loss of granular layer is the most consistent finding.

questions.q: A 32-year-old female presents with melasma refractory to topical hydroquinone 4% for 3 months. Wood's lamp shows accentuation. Which treatment combination is most effective?
opts: Triple combination cream (hydroquinone + tretinoin + fluocinolone acetonide)
Chemical peel with glycolic acid alone
questions.exp: Triple combination cream (Kligman's modified formula: 4% hydroquinone + 0.05% tretinoin + 0.01% fluocinolone acetonide) is the gold standard for epidermal melasma. Wood's lamp accentuation confirms epidermal type. Tretinoin inhibits melanocyte transfer, hydroquinone inhibits tyrosinase, and steroid reduces inflammation.

questions.q: A 20-year-old female presents with depigmented patches over the perioral area, periorbital area, and hands. The patches are chalk-white on Wood's lamp examination. Dermoscopy shows perifollicular pigmentation. What does the presence of perifollicular pigmentation suggest?
opts: Residual melanocytes and favorable prognosis for repigmentation
questions.exp: Perifollicular pigmentation (retained pigment around hair follicles) in vitiligo indicates residual melanocytes in follicular reservoir, suggesting favorable prognosis for repigmentation. Hair follicles serve as melanocyte reservoir for repigmentation therapy.

questions.q: A dermatologist performs patch testing on a 40-year-old female suspected of contact dermatitis. The patch tests are applied on the upper back for 48 hours, removed, and read at 72-96 hours. A reading of '++' indicates:
opts: Extreme positive (intense erythema, bullae, spreading reaction)
questions.exp: ICDRG (International Contact Dermatitis Research Group) grading: (-) negative, (?) doubtful (faint erythema), (+) weak positive (erythema + infiltration + papules), (++) strong positive (erythema + infiltration + papules + vesicles), (+++) extreme positive (bullae, spreading).

questions.q: A 55-year-old male with androgenetic alopecia presents requesting treatment. His Hamilton-Norwood grade is IV. He is hypertensive on treatment. Which treatment should be used cautiously?
questions.exp: Topical minoxidil causes vasodilation and can potentially exacerbate hypotension or interact with antihypertensive medications. While it is used cautiously, it is not absolutely contraindicated but requires blood pressure monitoring. Finasteride is the main concern in women of childbearing age.

questions.q: A 28-year-old pregnant female (28 weeks) presents with intensely pruritic urticarial papules and plaques in the abdominal striae, sparing the periumbilical area. Which is the most likely diagnosis?
opts: Pruritic urticarial papules and plaques of pregnancy (PUPPP)
questions.exp: PUPPP (Pruritic urticarial papules and plaques of pregnancy/Polymorphic eruption of pregnancy) begins in abdominal striae, characteristically SPARES the periumbilical area, occurs in primigravida, usually in 3rd trimester. Pemphigoid gestationis involves periumbilical area with DIF showing linear C3.

questions.q: A 62-year-old male presents with pruritic violaceous, polygonal, flat-topped papules over the flexor aspect of wrists and oral mucosa with white lacy streaks (Wickham striae). Which is TRUE regarding treatment?
opts: Dapsone is the drug of choice for erosive oral lichen planus
Hydroxychloroquine is used for erosive oral LP
questions.exp: Hydroxychloroquine is used for erosive/recalcitrant oral lichen planus. Topical steroids (clobetasol) are first-line for oral LP. Dapsone and PUVA can also be used. Cyclosporine mouthwash is effective for erosive oral LP.

questions.q: A patient with severe plaque psoriasis is started on methotrexate 15 mg weekly. Folic acid 5 mg weekly (on a different day) is co-prescribed. After 3 months, he develops macrocytic anemia and oral ulcers. The most appropriate immediate management is:
opts: Stop methotrexate and administer leucovorin (folinic acid)
questions.exp: Methotrexate toxicity (macrocytic anemia, mucositis/oral ulcers, hepatotoxicity) requires immediate cessation of MTX and administration of leucovorin (folinic acid/citrovorum factor) rescue which bypasses the dihydrofolate reductase blockade caused by MTX.

questions.q: A patient on dapsone for dermatitis herpetiformis develops pallor, shortness of breath, and dark-colored urine. His G6PD levels are found to be low. Which complication has occurred?
questions.exp: G6PD deficiency predisposes to dapsone-induced hemolytic anemia (most common adverse effect). Methemoglobinemia is another serious adverse effect of dapsone. Agranulocytosis is rare. All patients on dapsone should have baseline G6PD levels checked, especially in populations with high G6PD deficiency prevalence.

questions.q: A 50-year-old female presents with painful, recurrent oral ulcers (3-4 episodes/year), lasting 10-14 days, >1 cm in diameter, healing with scarring. She also has genital ulcers and uveitis. What is the most appropriate initial systemic treatment?
questions.exp: Behcet's disease (triple symptom complex of oral ulcers, genital ulcers, uveitis). Colchicine is first-line for mucocutaneous manifestations including recurrent oral aphthae in Behcet's. Azathioprine is used for severe systemic manifestations including uveitis and neurological involvement.

questions.q: A 45-year-old male presents with exquisitely tender, erythematous, indurated plaques with cribriform scarring over the lower legs. He has underlying inflammatory bowel disease. Biopsy shows neutrophilic infiltrate in dermis without vasculitis. What is the most likely diagnosis?
questions.exp: Pyoderma gangrenosum (PG) presents with rapidly progressing, painful ulcers with violaceous undermined edges on lower limbs, associated with IBD, RA, and hematologic malignancies. Pathergy phenomenon is positive. Biopsy shows neutrophilic dermatosis without vasculitis. Cribriform scarring on healing is characteristic.

questions.q: A 30-year-old male presents with well-defined, honey-colored crusted lesions over the face with surrounding erythema after a minor abrasion. Gram stain shows gram-positive cocci in clusters. First-line topical treatment for localized disease is:
questions.exp: Non-bullous impetigo (most common) is caused by S. aureus (gram-positive cocci in clusters) presenting with honey-colored crusted lesions. Topical mupirocin 2% is first-line for localized impetigo, applied 3x/day for 5 days. It has low resistance rates and good efficacy against both S. aureus and S. pyogenes.

questions.q: A 25-year-old presents for chemical peel for acne scars. The dermatologist decides on a superficial peel. Which agent penetrates only to the papillary dermis and is used for superficial peeling?
questions.exp: Chemical peel depth: Superficial (epidermis to papillary dermis) - glycolic acid 20-70%, salicylic acid, Jessner's solution, TCA 10-20%. Medium depth (papillary to mid-reticular dermis) - TCA 35%, combination peels. Deep (reticular dermis) - Baker-Gordon phenol peel, TCA >50%.

questions.q: A 40-year-old female presents with diffuse hair loss 3 months after delivery of her child. She notices 200-300 hairs on her pillow daily. Pull test is positive. What is the expected hair cycle phase showing increased percentage on trichogram?
questions.exp: Telogen effluvium (TE) following delivery (3 months postpartum) is caused by synchronized shift of anagen hairs to telogen phase due to hormonal changes. Trichogram shows increased telogen hairs (>25%, normally <15%). The trigger occurs 2-4 months before hair loss, correlating with postpartum timing.
